introduction: At Mars’s north polar edge, layered terrain and frost create boundaries that can resemble terrestrial geology.
observe: Trace the sharp boundary between light and dark terrain.
Compare broad layers with the finer surface texture.
explanation: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter recorded a chasm at the north polar cap edge, where strong downslope winds help carry sediment toward the Olympia Undae dune field.
colorMethod: This spacecraft image is processed to make surface structure legible; color should be read as imaging data, not as an unaided-eye view from the ground.
whyItMatters: Landforms alone do not identify a world. Instrument, location and scale turn visual similarity into evidence.
